slot_note: DA09 seed (START_HERE): the seed's world, decision and quantity kept (a software company's Data Engineer III base-pay midpoint for the bands taking effect on 1 April 2027, read from a salary-sharing platform's licensed extract as of the 1 October 2026 benchmark date); the seed's focus split is kept only as a lower rung (job matching) and the decisive step is re-found in the data: each report's pay ageing to the benchmark date
niche: a software company's compensation team setting its 2027 Data Engineer pay bands (25th percentile, median and 75th percentile of market base pay for each of four levels) from a salary-sharing platform's respondent reports filed over three years, each report's pay carried to the 1 October 2026 benchmark date
answer: File the Data Engineer III midpoint at $170,000 for the pay bands that take effect on 1 April 2027.
stakeholder_role: the company's head of total rewards

spine.entity: one row is one salary-platform respondent's current report (employer, title, platform family and level, employer level code, state, years of experience, base pay, the date the pay was reported, and for respondents who updated, the previous base pay and its date)

driver: The decisive quantity is a level at a reference date estimated from reports filed at earlier dates, each carried to the reference date by how the level itself moves at a fixed grade inside the same reporting units; the reporters' own changes between two reports run faster because individuals also climb within the grade, and the trend across the pooled reports runs slower because the units reporting at later dates sit lower, so carrying by the paired changes overshoots and carrying by the pooled trend, or not at all, undershoots.
driver_concrete: Each matched respondent's base pay is aged from the date it was reported to 1 October 2026 by the market movement for the job at a fixed level read within employers (an intercept for each employer and level), 2.7 per cent a year, before the medians and quartiles are taken; the re-reporters' own growth between their two reports (4.7 per cent) includes merit inside the level and over-ages every report, and the trend across the pooled reports (1.1 per cent) under-ages them because the employers whose engineers began filing later pay less at every level.
stump: A competent analyst matches the platform's respondents to Data Engineer III through the crosswalk and the focus table, sees the reports were filed over three years and carries each to the benchmark date at the re-reporters' own pay growth between their two reports at the same level (4.7 per cent a year), filing the midpoint at $175,000, because a person's raises carry the merit earned inside the level; the analyst who corrects that by the level's movement across the pooled reports (1.1 per cent a year) files $166,000, because the employers the platform reached later pay less at every level; carried by the movement within employers (2.7 per cent a year) the reports give $170,000, and left as filed they give $164,000.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who matches every respondent to the company's levels through the crosswalk and the focus table and reads every rule carries each report to the benchmark date at the re-reporters' own growth between their two reports at the same level (4.7 per cent a year) and files the Data Engineer III midpoint at $175,000; one who reads the level's movement across the pooled reports files $166,000; one who leaves the reports as filed files $164,000; carrying them by how pay at the fixed level moves within employers (2.7 per cent a year) files the golden $170,000.
domain_test: The call turns on the market median base pay for a job and level as in effect on a benchmark date, read from pay reports filed at different dates, which compensation practice ages to the date by the market movement at a fixed level (the structure movement) measured on matched employers, the way the Employment Cost Index holds establishments fixed, rather than by individuals' raises, which carry merit, or by the pooled reports' trend, which carries the platform's changing employer mix; with a hospital's or a utility's nouns there is no job-level band, no re-reporter progressing inside it and no salary platform whose reach widens to lower-paying employers, and the task stops reading the same.
layer1: a salary platform's own job family and normalised level mixing roles and levels the company's architecture separates (machine-learning data engineers inside data engineering; employer level codes mapped through an effective-dated crosswalk)
respondent reports filed over three years, a share carrying the respondent's previous report
free-text titles and employer names in several spellings
OEWS state employment margins beside the platform's respondents
ask paths: an HRIS roster with rehires under a second employee id, contractors and effective-dated job changes; a posting system export listing multi-location postings once per city

differentiation.task87: task87 caps a delivered count under an exclusivity no procedure states; this build ages pay reports to a reference date by the level's own movement rather than the reporters' progression: no cap, no exclusivity, no filed procedure
differentiation.task445: task445 completes a period total for reporters whose reports have not arrived by carrying each from its last report; this build has every report in hand and ages each one to a reference date by the market's movement at a fixed level, not by the reporters' own progression
differentiation.task256: task256 transfers a reference survey's joint body-size distribution to a roster through the survey's conditional distribution within sex; this build reads a rate of change at a fixed grade inside the same reporting employers because the platform's employers change across dates: a time trend's composition, not a population transfer
differentiation.task259: loop 1 keeps loop 0's carry by the level's own movement and reads that movement inside employers: loop 0's decisive trend across the pooled reports is now a rung, wrong because the platform's employers arrive through the window paying less at every level

lineage.architecture: v1 (loop 0): the level's movement read across the pooled reports as the decisive rung
lineage.fate: hardened at the author's request for a second layer (2026-10-13, before any portal result); kept as rung R3 of loop 1, where the platform's employers arrive through the window paying less and the pooled movement (1.1 per cent) files $166,000
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a level at a reference date estimated from reports filed at earlier dates, each of which has to be carried to the reference date by how the level itself moves at a fixed grade; the reporters' own changes between their two reports run faster because individuals also climb within the grade, so carrying the reports by the paired changes overshoots and leaving them as filed undershoots.
